steps.a: Binary floats can't represent 0.1 exactly, so multiplying by 1000.0 leaks the error into the label. The amounts come in as strings from the prescription feed, so I'll carry them as Decimal end to end and quantize only when formatting.

steps.a: Done. Unit conversion now uses Decimal factors and accepts strings or Decimals, and labels are formatted with normalize, so 0.1 mg shows as 100 mcg. Doses per day became an int (it was only ever a whole count), which fixed the one mixed Decimal/float multiply. All 412 tests pass.

reference.summary: Fixed a floating point error in medication unit conversion that printed 100.00000000000001 mcg on labels by switching the conversion factors and amounts to Decimal and normalising when formatting; a follow-on type error in the daily total was fixed by making doses per day an integer, and the full test suite passes.
facts: The conversion multiplied binary floats, so 0.1 mg became 100.00000000000001 mcg
Factors and amounts now use Decimal and labels normalise the value
A Decimal times float TypeError in the daily total surfaced and was fixed by making doses per day an int
